## 🤖 AI review — `ai-review:pass`

> ⚠️ **This PR modifies the AI-review machinery (`.github/`/`scripts/`) — the code review still ran; its honest verdict is `ai-review:pass` (above), but a human must review because a gate cannot certify a change to itself.**
>
> The code-review verdict is reported AS-IS — it is **not** masked as `ai-review:changes` (#596), so a genuine reviewer-requested change on a machinery PR still surfaces distinctly. Auto-merge is held by a SEPARATE human gate instead: the `needs-human-review` label, the `machinery-review-required` check, and `ready-to-merge` staying red (no SHA-bound pass witness is posted for a machinery PR).

### Reviewer
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Correctly fixes #2233 (anchored CLI-notice classifier + meter second-witness veto); state propagates in-shell, fail-closed paths preserved, invariants intact, thoroughly tested.
findings:
- low scripts/drain-inbox.sh:296-330 (is_quota / QUOTA_NOTICE_RE) — The drain no longer shares ai-review-guard.js's isQuotaExhaustion; it now maintains its own hardcoded list of CLI wall/rate-limit forms. This deliberately abandons the prior 'bash and JS must not drift' single-source-of-truth. It is justified (the drain classifies whole merged streams where review-branch.sh splits stderr/stdout) and a missed text signal is backstopped by the independent quota_gate meter, but the two classifiers now need parallel maintenance if Anthropic changes the wall wording…
- low scripts/drain-inbox.sh:_quota_notice_forms (form: You've (hit|reached) your ([^ ]+ ){0,4}(limit|budget)) — An UNFENCED, column-0 line of model prose beginning like 'You've hit your goal limit ...' would still match (up to 4 words allowed between 'your' and 'limit'). The diff explicitly acknowledges this residual (the honest-limit note) and relies on the meter contradiction check to shorten any resulting false pause, so it is bounded, not silent. No change required.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Security (code changed)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: No security or blocking correctness issues: no secrets, no new network/credential surface, offline posture preserved; the quota-classifier rewrite is well-anchored, tested, and fails closed.
findings:
- low scripts/drain-inbox.sh:304-360 (quota_notice_lines / is_quota) — The change replaces the shared JS classifier (ai-review-guard.js isQuotaExhaustion) with a bash-native anchored regex, reintroducing the bash/JS drift the old comment forbade. This is intentional and well-justified (the drain classifies a merged stdout+stderr stream while review-branch.sh splits streams), but the two classifiers can now diverge on what counts as a session-limit signal; no shared test pins them together. Non-blocking.
- low scripts/drain-inbox.sh:352-358 (quota_notice_lines awk fence toggle) — The awk fenced-block stripper toggles state on each ```/~~~ line; an unbalanced (odd) fence in untrusted child output leaves `fenced` true for the remainder, which would strip a subsequent genuine column-0 wall line and yield a false-negative (real quota treated as a crash). Fails safe (loop stops after MAX_FAILURES rather than spinning), and the pre-change behavior had the opposite (false-positive) problem, so this is an acceptable tradeoff. Non-blocking.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Architect (design / scope)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Architecturally coherent, in-scope dev-tooling fix; fails closed, control flow sound, only a non-blocking note on the classifier divergence lacking a DR.
findings:
- non-blocking scripts/drain-inbox.sh:~110 (removal of GUARD / is_quota rewrite) — The change reverses a documented design invariant — the base code kept the quota classifier as a single source of truth shared with review-branch.sh via ai-review-guard.js's isQuotaExhaustion ('Reused, never re-implemented — bash and JS must not drift'). It now re-implements a distinct anchored/shape-based classifier (QUOTA_NOTICE_RE) in bash. The rationale is sound (merged stream vs splittable stream) and it is confined to Tier-0 dev tooling and reversible in <1 day, so not a blocking missing-…
- non-blocking scripts/drain-inbox.sh:quota_signal_backoff_sleep (overruled arm resets QUOTA_CONTRADICTED_STREAK=0) — For a genuinely persistent, meter-blind wall (e.g. a per-model cap the oauth reading cannot see), the streak resets on 'overruled', so the loop oscillates contradicted->overruled->contradicted rather than settling to fail-closed, dispatching-and-crashing roughly every other cycle. The waste is bounded by QUOTA_CONTRADICT_MAX and tunable, and the alternative (never reset) would permanently disable the veto after one transient contradiction — so the tradeoff is defensible and documented, but wort…
- non-blocking scripts/drain-inbox.sh:quota_notice_lines (awk fence-stripping) — An unterminated markdown fence in a child's captured output would drop all subsequent lines before grep, so a genuine column-0 wall line appearing after a stray unmatched ``` would be missed and the drain would not pause. Low risk because the CLI never fences its own notice and prints it at column 0, and downstream meter/streak logic bounds the impact; acceptable as documented, but a latent edge.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Skeptic (evidence discipline)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Claims are backed by real, asserting tests with controls; referenced functions and verdict wording verified in drain-inbox.sh; root-cause (classifier + second-witness gate) fixed, not data-patched.
findings:
- minor scripts/drain-inbox.sh:~is_quota comment block — Rationale comment asserts a mechanism about a sibling file — 'review-branch.sh solved the same bug (#1131, #1155) by splitting stderr from stdout' — which is unverified within this diff (plausible-inference-not-observation per widened RCDD). Non-blocking: it is rationale prose, not a status/completion claim, and nothing load-bearing depends on it.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

_Independent fresh-context reviewers (`scripts/review-branch.sh`, no-tools agents reading the diff as untrusted data); each label decided by the deterministic fail-closed gate (`scripts/review-decide.sh`). Posted by `minspec-sdd[bot]` from CI — provenance is the App identity, verified here, not the label alone (#428, #342). Coverage `panel` — voters that ran: **reviewer + security + architect + skeptic**. The combined verdict fails toward `changes` if ANY voter requests changes._

<!-- ai-review-guard:staleness -->
**`ai-review:pass` stripped — new commits (#359).**

new commits were pushed after ai-review:pass — the greenlight is stale. A fresh independent review must re-apply `ai-review:pass` before `ready-to-merge` goes green again.

Follow-up commit `2cfcebf3` addresses three of the AI review's non-blocking findings. Each has a test that failed first:

- **Unbalanced fence** (security, architect): fences are now paired in order, and only a closed pair hides anything. An unclosed fence earlier in a capture no longer hides a later genuine wall. Test: `drain-continuous.test.ts`, "an UNCLOSED fence earlier in a capture cannot hide a genuine wall after it".
- **Streak oscillation** (architect): the contradiction streak now resets only when a cycle completes cleanly. A meter-blind cap therefore costs `MINSPEC_QUOTA_CONTRADICT_MAX` extra launches in total, not one per long sleep. Test: `drain-quota-signal-loop.test.ts`, "once overruled, the veto stays spent across the long sleep".
- **Unverified sibling claim** (skeptic): the rationale comment now names `review-branch.sh`'s `quota_failure`, so it can be checked.

Deliberately not changed: the drain's classifier no longer being shared with `ai-review-guard.js` (flagged by reviewer, security and architect). The divergence is intended. The drain classifies a merged stream that the review path can split. Also, `ai-review-guard.js` is byte-synced into a template shipped to adopters, so moving the matcher there would widen this fix to adopters' repos. No DR, because the change is reversible in under a day (the DR-359 filter). The next consumer, SPEC-074's planned dispatch classification, is tracked in #2237.

Re-verified at `2cfcebf3`: all 17 drain suites (341 tests), the swallowed-gate lint, and the full `npx vitest run` (317 files, 6,550 passed).

Response to the architect voter on `99e1daa5` (the other three voters pass). I am not pushing again for this, because what remains is a decision for the founder, not a code defect.

- **High (FR-6 second witness): I believe this is a misreading, and I checked it against the spec text.** SPEC-074's FR-6 says the drain "reads dispatch-issue.sh's *entire* stdout ... and will therefore continue to detect the outage and pause the drain cycle, unchanged". AC-7 tests exactly that with the AC-1 fixture, `You've hit your session limit · resets 1pm (Australia/Sydney)`. That is the CLI's own line. `dispatch-issue.sh` tees `claude`'s output to its stdout at column 0 (`claude -p ... 2>&1 | tee "$LOG"`), and SPEC-074 does not change that. So this matcher detects the outage whether or not an FR-4 echo is also present. It is also the more independent witness of the two: it reads the CLI's line, not dispatch's own verdict echo, which FR-6 describes as "not a hand-off".
- **Blocking (the departure from SPEC-074, with no DR): this is a real governance question, and it needs the founder.** The departure is recorded in the code where the fork happens, and in #2237 with a recommendation and its cost. It cannot be resolved inside this PR's file scope. The options are: amend SPEC-074's FR-1 and AC-6 (voids its approval), write a DR recording the reversal, or move the matcher into `ai-review-guard.js` (which would also mean regenerating the adopter template that file is byte-synced into). The DR-359 filter does not require a DR here, because the change is reversible in under a day. Whether one is wanted anyway is part of the #2237 decision.
- **Low (`MINSPEC_DRAIN_REMEDIATE` override):** dev-time only. `scripts/drain-inbox.sh` is not in any shipped template, so the override cannot reach an adopter.

CI is green at `99e1daa5` (test, lint, build, e2e, package, gate, gitleaks, actionlint, validation).

commits.messageBody:
… a fresh meter veto the long sleep

Root cause: is_quota ran ai-review-guard.js's loose isQuotaExhaustion (a bare
`quota`, `429`, `rate limit`, `too many requests`) over each child's whole 2>&1
stream, which also carries the echoed issue title, git's `HEAD is now at
<subject>` and the model's prose, so content that only mentioned quota paused
the drain; and quota_sleep_secs then slept to the 5h resets_at without reading
the percentage beside it, so a fresh 0% reading could neither veto nor shorten
the pause.

Classification: the drain now matches only the Claude CLI's own limit,
rate-limit and overload lines - anchored at column 0, outside markdown code
fences, CR treated as a line end - in the forms the CLI itself builds (the
wall-prefix list in Claude Code 2.1.283, plus older CLI forms and the CLI's
API Error lines). The three false pauses of 2026-09-30 are no longer signals:
the #2178 (SPEC-078 spec) dispatch at 16:38, the #2226 (SPEC-078 spec PR)
remediation at 18:11 and the #1060 (ai-review:paused) dispatch at 19:03. The
one genuine wall that day, #1785's, still is. The wall publisher now parses
only those lines, never the whole capture.

Second witness: after a text-only signal the loop force-refreshes the meter
and asks quota_gate's own verdict. A fresh reading with room in every window
contradicts the signal: the drain logs that and backs off
MINSPEC_QUOTA_CONTRADICTED_BACKOFF (60s) instead of sleeping to the reset,
and does not write a 100% wall reading over that reading. A stale or missing
reading keeps the old fail-closed sleep. The veto is bounded by
MINSPEC_QUOTA_CONTRADICT_MAX (1) contradicted signals in a row, then it fails
closed, so a cap the meter cannot see costs one extra launch, not the queue.

Tests: T3 regressions with the verbatim captures as fixtures
(drain-continuous, drain-quota-deadline, including a T0 check that the veto
agrees with quota_gate on every reading), and drain-quota-signal-loop, which
drives the real continuous loop on the serial, parallel and remediation
paths. ai-review-guard.js is untouched, so the review path is unchanged.
